overview: This resolution, agreed to by both the House and Senate, sets up a joint session of Congress, a meeting of both chambers together in the House chamber, on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, at 9 p.m. The purpose is to hear a message from the President, the kind of joint session typically used for the annual State of the Union address. Congress gave final approval on February 12, 2026.
for: Supporters say it is the standard way to give the President a formal opportunity to address Congress and the nation.
against: Critics say it is a routine scheduling measure that does not change any law or spending.
